```{r}
devtools::clean_dll()
devtools::load_all()
```

## failed cases 
```{r}
# input validation, invalid component names
visualize_cost(
  component_names = c(4, 5),
  unit_costs = c(1.2, 2.4),
  default_cost_fxn_type = "linear",
  intervention_lower_bounds = c(1, 0),
  intervention_upper_bounds = c(4, 40)
)
```

## success cases 
```{r}
# linear default cost
visualize_cost(
  component_names = c("gear", "qsec"),
  unit_costs = c(1.2, 2.4),
  default_cost_fxn_type = "linear",
  intervention_lower_bounds = c(1, 0),
  intervention_upper_bounds = c(4, 40)
)
```

```{r}
# cubic default cost
visualize_cost(
  component_names = c("gear", "qsec"),
  unit_costs = c(2, 5),
  default_cost_fxn_type = "cubic",
  intervention_lower_bounds = c(1, 0),
  intervention_upper_bounds = c(4, 40)
)
```

```{r}
# cubic default cost, more components
visualize_cost(
  component_names = c("gear", "qsec", "disp", "hp"),
  unit_costs = c(2, 5, 3, 1.2),
  default_cost_fxn_type = "cubic",
  intervention_lower_bounds = c(1, 0, 10, 0),
  intervention_upper_bounds = c(4, 40, 20, 10)
)
```
## custom slider ranges (issue #34)
```{r}
# Each coefficient slider now gets its own default range scaled to the
# coefficient's magnitude (via compute_slider_range), instead of a fixed
# -15..15 range. Launch and confirm: the high-order cubic coefficients (small
# values) have narrow usable ranges while the leading coefficient has a wider
# range, and each slider has "Range min" / "Range max" inputs above it for
# setting a custom range. Editing a Range input rescales only that slider;
# "Reset Coefficients" restores both the values and the default ranges.
visualize_cost(
  component_names = c("Counseling", "HomeBP"),
  unit_costs = c(2, 5),
  default_cost_fxn_type = "cubic",
  intervention_lower_bounds = c(0, 0),
  intervention_upper_bounds = c(10, 10)
)
```
